title: P2-14a storage-batch: Extend RuntimeJournal::append_sequenced to accept &[RuntimeJournalEvent] and use JournalWriteBatch::commit
description: Feature P2-14a (split from black-hat-revised vb-8fbja). Black-hat review round 1 found that the original P2-14 had 4 sub-phases in one bead, violating Farley's 'smallest change' rule. This bead (P2-14a) handles sub-phase (14a) only: extend the RuntimeJournal::append_sequenced trait method to accept a slice of events, and use JournalWriteBatch::commit for atomicity. Real source: crates/vb_runtime/src/journal/chunk_001.rs:222, chunk_002.rs:294-315, chunk_003.rs:8 — three implementations of append_sequenced, each taking a single RuntimeJournalEvent and calling self.append_storage_event. The new signature: `fn append_sequenced(&self, events: &[RuntimeJournalEvent], seq: &[EventSeq]) -> RuntimeResult<()>`. The new body constructs a JournalWriteBatch from vb_storage::batch.rs:46-62 and commits it once. No coalescing (that's P2-14b); no A/B benchmark (that's P2-14c). Master §61 atomicity invariant: all events in the slice are persisted atomically or none are. Kani harness: prove append_sequenced on a slice of N events results in either 0 or N persisted events, never partial. proptest: 100 random (slice, seq) pairs assert atomicity.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL expose append_sequenced that accepts &[RuntimeJournalEvent] for batched commits
THE SYSTEM SHALL use JournalWriteBatch::commit for atomicity when the slice is non-empty

event_driven.trigger: WHEN append_sequenced is called with a slice of 100 events and 100 sequence numbers
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL construct a JournalWriteBatch and commit it in a single Fjall transaction; either all 100 events persist or none do

unwanted.condition: IF the slice and seq slices have different lengths
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT panic; it must return Err(LengthMismatch)
unwanted.because: Pre-condition violation is a typed error, not a panic

unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT partially apply the batch; it must roll back and return BatchCommitFailed
unwanted.because: Master §61: atomicity is non-negotiable; partial application violates the contract

preconditions: JournalWriteBatch is fully implemented at vb_storage::batch.rs:46-62
The 3 existing append_sequenced implementations (chunk_001.rs:222, chunk_002.rs:294, chunk_003.rs:8) are the only callers
postconditions: RuntimeJournal::append_sequenced has a new signature accepting &[RuntimeJournalEvent] and &[EventSeq]
All 3 implementations use JournalWriteBatch::commit instead of per-event append_storage_event
No regression: existing call sites that pass a single event via a 1-element slice still work
invariants: Atomicity: N events in the slice produce 0 or N persisted events, never partial (master §61)
Sequence numbers remain monotonic per run (master §68.5)

happy: append_sequenced_with_100_events_commits_atomically: 100 events in 1 call; assert 1 Fjall commit (not 100)
append_sequenced_with_1_event_works: a 1-element slice still works (regression for single-event call sites)
error: append_sequenced_with_commit_failure_rolls_back: force a commit failure; assert 0 events persisted (not partial)
edge: append_sequenced_with_empty_slice_is_noop: events.len() == 0; assert Ok(()) and no Fjall write
proptest_append_sequenced_atomicity: 100 random (slice, seq) pairs; assert either 0 or all events persist
kani_append_sequenced_atomicity: bounded model check with 4 event types and 4 commit failure scenarios

files: crates/vb_runtime/src/journal/chunk_002.rs:294-315 (StorageRuntimeJournal::append_sequenced — the second impl; the one with action_index_update)
patterns: Pattern: existing per-event call sites use the single-event signature; the new slice-based signature is additive (the old one is removed only after all callers migrate)
questions: Should the old single-event signature be kept as a wrapper, or removed after migration? Recommend: keep as a wrapper that constructs a 1-element slice and calls the new method; this minimizes churn

data_integrity_failures.failure: A commit failure mid-batch leaves half the events persisted and half not; recovery reads a partial journal and rebuilds a wrong frame
data_integrity_failures.prevention: JournalWriteBatch::commit is atomic; on failure, the entire batch rolls back

security_failures.failure: Attacker exploits a length mismatch between events and seqs to bypass the sequence-number invariant
security_failures.prevention: Length mismatch returns a typed LengthMismatch error before any commit is attempted
